To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated that the electrochemical modification of carbon and chromium surfaces allows the direct imaging of a dsDNA-transposase protein complex by AFM.
we have developed a method to image the interaction between DNA and a protein by means of atomic force microscopy.
we developed a new surface for the immobilization of DNA molecules and we have used it to image the interaction of a transposable element with its target DNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of an electrochemical method to prepare organic monolayers for the study of the transposase-DNS complex.
the development of a new method of chemical functionalization of carbon and chromium surfaces, and the application of this surface to study the interaction between DNA and protein by AFM imaging.
the development of new strategies for the modification of surfaces and their use for the study of the interaction of proteins with nucleic acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transposase protein interacts with its target dsDNAs in a specific manner, and this is the first direct observation of this kind of complex by AFM imaging.
the electrochemical method used to modify a surface with a monolayer of a diazonum salt followed by activation with PCl(5) is a powerful and versatile tool for the study of protein-DNA interactions.

the electrochemical modification of carbon and chromium surfaces by diazonium salts is an effective way to obtain surfaces that are suitable for the immobilization of DNA and the investigation of its interactions with proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrochemically modified carbon surface can be used to study the interaction between dsDNA and transposase.

the organic layer formed by electrochemical reduction and activation of sulfanilic is a good candidate for the immobilization of DNA molecules on carbon and chromium electrodes and for the study of protein-DNA interactions.
the electrochemical reduction of diazonium salts on carbon and chromium surfaces provides a simple, fast, and reproducible method to form an organic monolayer with a high degree of compactness.

the electrochemical modification of carbon and chromium surfaces with Ar-SO(2)-Cl allows us to immobilize dsDNA for AFM imaging and the study of its interaction with transposases.
the organic monolayer is a very useful tool for the study of DNA-protein interaction.
